snippet.title: Faith, Truth, and Cultural Confusion: Getting the Bible Right Again
snippet.description:
In this episode, we briefly reflect on Easter and the reality that doubt has always surrounded the resurrection, just as it did for people like Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea.

The core of the conversation centers on how truth is being handled today. We unpack the difference between misusing Scripture and distorting it, and why that distinction matters. Looking at real cultural examples, we talk about how the Bible is often used to support ideas it was never meant to, and what it looks like to interpret it faithfully.

We also explore the tension of boldness and wisdom in young believers and the importance of real discipleship. Passion without formation can lead to unnecessary harm, even when the intent is right.

Finally, we address a deeper issue many men are facing today. Without affirmation and direction, men often withdraw or react in unhealthy ways. What does it look like to call men up and form them with truth and purpose?

This episode is a call to hold firmly to truth while intentionally developing people to live it out well.
